title: Human action gates
summary: A recipe step typed operator_gate human_action is the non-self-approving gate for a step only the person may do. Its human_purpose is one of machine_approval, private_invite_entry or company_sign_in. The contract refuses keys, ready_text, wait_seconds and any other field, so the step cannot type into the terminal or carry a secret; gate_timeout_seconds bounds the wait at 1..1800. The gate prints one machine_qa.operator_gate line with kind human_action, self_approving false, the purpose, where the person acts (the visible Terminal window or its tmux attach command) and instructions. A machine_approval gate names the displayed match code (the shared MATCH_CODE_PATTERN format) and the yoke machines approve CODE command for the person's already-connected machine; a company_sign_in gate names the code the teammate approves in the browser; either refuses human_action_context_missing when no match code is on screen. An invite entry tells the inviter to run yoke invite NAME and never names or receives the code. The gate then only reads the terminal: completion_text passes; a denial or expiry fails as human_action_rejected; a setup exit fails as terminal_setup_exited; an expired wait fails as human_action_timed_out; a failed lease renewal fails as human_action_heartbeat_failed; each names a recovery. The step evidence records human_action with the purpose, waited_seconds and self_approving false. On Linux only machine_browser_approval and company_sign_in start the desktop Chromium; approval and invite steps run on a host without a desktop.
